## Motivation

Extend the CUDA TileLang raw FP8 KV path added in #42957. Kernel dispatch currently accepts packed rows and CUDA-incompatible E4M3FNUZ tensors until a lower-level failure; attention CP is not rejected by the raw-layout validation. CUDA raw KV writes also use separate casts before scattering despite an existing fused writer.

## Modifications

- Reject FP8 KV rows whose width differs from the query and reject E4M3FNUZ on CUDA before kernel dispatch.
- Validate resolved `attn_cp_size` alongside the existing DCP constraint, retaining the existing mixed-backend and HiSparse checks.
- Select the fused cast/paged writer by raw versus scaled layout, including NoPE-only inputs with no RoPE tensor.
- Add numerical, masking, negative-control and page-boundary coverage, plus a model-accuracy report and sampled IDs/hashes. The raw layout remains unscaled; this does not add support for group-scaled packed KV rows.

The earlier raw-layout CUDA approach is documented in #36904. Already merged allocator/backend routing and the existing NoPE kernel logic are retained rather than duplicated.

## Accuracy Tests

**Real sampled evaluation: GLM-5.3-Flash-FP8, raw `fp8_e4m3` KV, TileLang prefill/decode, TP8/EP4 + MTP, 8×H20-96GB.** EvalScope 1.12.0; temperature 0, top_p 1, seed 42, native chat template/default thinking, one candidate per sample, concurrency 8.

| Dataset / metric | Correct / scored | Score | Input TPS | Input TPS/GPU |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| IFEval strict prompt | 35/40 | 87.50% | N/A | N/A |
| C-Eval validation | 50/52 | 96.15% | N/A | N/A |
| GSM8K | 48/50 | 96.00% | N/A | N/A |
| LiveCodeBench release_v6 pass@1 | 16/18 | 88.89% | N/A | N/A |

Accuracy-only: input/output/total TPS are unavailable. IFEval loose prompt was 90.00%, strict instruction 56/61=91.80%, and loose instruction 57/61=93.44%.

Samples were selected without replacement using seed 42: IFEval by instruction-count strata (0-shot), C-Eval one per all 52 subjects (5-shot), GSM8K uniform (4-shot), and LiveCodeBench six per difficulty (0-shot; easy 6/6, medium 6/6, hard 4/6). LiveCodeBench's equal-difficulty sample is not a population-weighted full-dataset score.

All 160 selected samples were scored. One C-Eval and one LiveCodeBench response exhausted the respective 32768/65536-token output budgets without a final answer; both count as incorrect. The other failed code sample raised `IndexError`. No API/transport failures occurred. A sampled evaluator cache-ID mismatch was repaired and request/prediction/review identities audited; two historical duplicate requests remain in the 162 actual requests, with no correctness-based response selection.

**Provenance/scope:** the model evaluation was completed on runtime base `7760d5264ac16b85392aefb1bf5c13ce38d9632e` with validation patch `f9c6b44d964504c6ab9e0088c090aa8a10a5ff5e`, not rerun on this PR's latest upstream base. There is no paired BF16 KV accuracy control or full-dataset accuracy claim. Full settings, failure treatment, source IDs and hashes are in the [validation report](https://github.com/gitover22/sglang/blob/26f3713b588632db271388d34864d3dffe0b4406/test/manual/kernels/README.glm53_tilelang_fp8.md) and its machine-readable summary.

**Rebased component validation:** on H20 SM90, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 and TileLang 0.1.12, the exact committed Python files passed **15 tests and 9 subtests**. Tests cover NoPE/RoPE, 8/16/32 heads, quantized-input FP32 references, one-hot and all-masked rows, wrong-index negative control, invalid layouts/formats, page boundaries and exported buffer lengths. The two CP regression assertions fail against the pre-fix upstream override code and pass with this patch.

```bash
python -m pytest -v \
  test/registered/unit/test_dsa_tilelang_fp8_validation.py \
  test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_tilelang_dsa_fp8_cuda.py \
  test/registered/mem_cache/test_tilelang_raw_fp8_pool.py
```

All changed-file pre-commit checks passed. Full-tree non-Rust checks passed; unrelated Rust hooks could not run because the local Rust toolchain is unavailable.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No new end-to-end serving benchmark or profile was run for this upstream port, and no throughput gain is claimed. The raw writer uses the existing fused cast/write kernel instead of separate casts and scatter. For a 512-dimensional NoPE row, raw FP8 stores 512 bytes versus BF16's 1024 bytes; this describes row storage, not a measured serving speedup.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add focused registered numerical and runtime tests.
- [x] Update validation documentation.
- [x] Provide real sampled accuracy results with runtime and sampling limitations.
- [ ] Provide a fresh paired end-to-end speed benchmark/profile.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

+# CUDA TileLang raw FP8 KV validation
+
+Use both `--dsa-prefill-backend tilelang` and `--dsa-decode-backend tilelang`
+with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`. CUDA FP8 Tensor Cores (SM89+) are required.
+The raw layout has no per-block scales; it is distinct from the scaled,
+packed layout consumed by other CUDA DSA backends. Mixed backends, DCP,
+attention CP and HiSparse are unsupported for this CUDA path.
+
+CUDA routing is already supported by [PR #42957](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/42957).
+The earlier raw-layout approach was described in
+[PR #36904](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36904).
+The additional checks reject packed rows and ROCm's E4M3FNUZ format on CUDA.
+The paged writer fuses the cast to raw FP8 with the write, including NoPE-only
+rows where the RoPE input is absent.
+
+## Component tests
+
+```bash
+python -m pytest -v \
+  test/registered/unit/test_dsa_tilelang_fp8_validation.py \
+  test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_tilelang_dsa_fp8_cuda.py \
+  test/registered/mem_cache/test_tilelang_raw_fp8_pool.py
+```
+
+Kernel references use the same quantized inputs as the kernel, isolating
+kernel correctness from quantization error. Coverage includes NoPE/RoPE,
+8/16/32 heads, padded sparse indices, exact one-hot reads, all-masked rows,
+an FP32 attention reference and a wrong-index negative control. Pool tests
+check page-boundary writes, untouched rows and exported buffer byte lengths.
+These component checks do not establish end-to-end PD transfer correctness.
+
+## Sampled model accuracy
+
+The following is a real evaluation performed on October 13, 2026 using
+GLM-5.3-Flash-FP8, raw `fp8_e4m3` KV, TileLang prefill/decode and 8 H20-96GB
+GPUs. The evaluated runtime was base commit
+`7760d5264ac16b85392aefb1bf5c13ce38d9632e` with validation patch
+`f9c6b44d964504c6ab9e0088c090aa8a10a5ff5e`. These model-level results have
+not been rerun on the latest upstream base of this PR.
+
+| Dataset / metric | Correct / scored | Score | Input TPS | Input TPS/GPU |
+| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
+| IFEval strict prompt | 35/40 | 87.50% | N/A | N/A |
+| C-Eval validation | 50/52 | 96.15% | N/A | N/A |
+| GSM8K | 48/50 | 96.00% | N/A | N/A |
+| LiveCodeBench release_v6 pass@1 | 16/18 | 88.89% | N/A | N/A |
+
+TPS fields are unavailable because this was an accuracy evaluation, not a
+serving throughput measurement. Output TPS and total TPS are also unavailable.
+All 160 selected samples remain in the denominators. IFEval loose prompt was
+36/40 (90.00%), strict instruction 56/61 (91.80%), and loose instruction
+57/61 (93.44%). LiveCodeBench was easy 6/6, medium 6/6 and hard 4/6.
+
+Sampling used seed 42 without replacement: IFEval 40/541 proportionally
+stratified by instruction count (0-shot), C-Eval 52/1346 with one sample per
+subject (5-shot), GSM8K 50/1319 (4-shot), and LiveCodeBench 18/1055 with six
+per difficulty (0-shot). The equal-difficulty LiveCodeBench sample is not a
+population-weighted full-dataset score.
+
+EvalScope 1.12.0 scored the model's native chat template and default thinking
+mode. Generation used temperature 0, top_p 1, seed 42, one candidate,
+non-streaming requests and concurrency 8. The output budget, including
+reasoning, was 32768 tokens for IFEval/C-Eval/GSM8K and 65536 for
+LiveCodeBench. The code sandbox had no network, host mounts or GPU, and used
+two CPUs, 4 GiB memory and a six-second limit per code test.
+
+Two samples exhausted the output budget without a final answer: C-Eval
+`law` source index 6 and LiveCodeBench source index 965. Both count as
+incorrect; neither was excluded or regenerated. The other failed
+LiveCodeBench sample, source index 46, raised `IndexError` in generated
+code. No API/transport failures occurred.
+
+The initial sampled loader exposed an evaluator cache-ID mismatch. After
+repair, dense evaluator IDs were mapped back to source IDs and complete
+request hashes were audited against predictions and reviews. Two duplicate
+historical requests remain in the request count (162 actual requests for
+160 unique scored samples). Reused responses were selected by complete
+request identity and first successful return, independently of correctness;
+the invalid initial scoring output was not used.
+
+There was no paired BF16 KV accuracy control. These sampled scores do not
+measure an accuracy delta caused by FP8 KV or certify full-dataset accuracy.
+Selected source IDs, sample hashes, exact scores and runtime metadata are in
+[the machine-readable summary](glm53_tilelang_fp8_accuracy_sample.json).
+
+## Evaluated serving configuration
+
+PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, CUDA 13.0, TileLang 0.1.12 and Transformers 5.19.0;
+FP8 weights, BF16 activations and FP32 SSM state. This was a single-host
+deployment, not PD disaggregation. The resolved chunk size was 8192;
+speculative `NEXTN` resolved to `EAGLE` with no adaptive speculation.
+
+```bash
+sglang serve --model-path "$MODEL_PATH" \
+  --tp-size 8 --ep-size 4 \
+  --mem-fraction-static 0.72 --max-running-requests 32 \
+  --dsa-prefill-backend tilelang --dsa-decode-backend tilelang \
+  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm \
+  --disable-shared-experts-fusion \
+  --speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 5 \
+  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 \
+  --reasoning-parser glm45 --tool-call-parser glm47 \
+  --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 32 --max-mamba-cache-size 384 \
+  --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-host-memory-mode cache \
+  --hicache-ratio 1 --hicache-write-policy write_back \
+  --hicache-io-backend kernel --hicache-mem-layout page_first \
+  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 31000 --enable-metrics --enable-cache-report
+```
+
+`MODEL_PATH` points to the original GLM-5.3-Flash-FP8 weights. The command
+records the evaluated runtime; it is not an assertion that every option is
+unchanged on future releases. No throughput improvement is implied by these
+accuracy or component tests.

+"""CUDA raw-FP8 DSA: NoPE/RoPE, TP head counts, padded KPool tails and masks.
+
+References use the same quantized inputs as the kernel, isolating kernel
+correctness from model-level quantization accuracy. A wrong-index control
+must fail the comparator rather than merely executing successfully.
+"""
+
+import unittest
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsa.tilelang_kernel import tilelang_sparse_fwd
+from sglang.srt.utils import is_hip
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=180, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
+
+
+def _reference(q, kv, indices, scale, d_v):
+    rows = indices[:, 0].long()
+    valid = rows >= 0
+    selected = kv.float()[rows.clamp_min(0), 0]
+    scores = torch.einsum("thd,tkd->thk", q.float(), selected) * scale
+    scores.masked_fill_(~valid[:, None], float("-inf"))
+    probabilities = torch.softmax(scores, dim=-1)
+    return torch.einsum("thk,tkd->thd", probabilities, selected[..., :d_v])
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(
+    torch.cuda.is_available()
+    and not is_hip()
+    and torch.cuda.get_device_capability() >= (8, 9),
+    "requires CUDA FP8 Tensor Cores",
+)
+class TestTileLangDsaFp8Cuda(CustomTestCase):
+    def _inputs(self, heads, d_v, d_tail, topk=2112):
+        torch.manual_seed(17)
+        tokens, pool_size = 5, 4096
+        dim = d_v + d_tail
+        q = (torch.randn(tokens, heads, dim, device="cuda") * 0.5).bfloat16()
+        kv = (torch.randn(pool_size, 1, dim, device="cuda") * 0.5).to(
+            torch.float8_e4m3fn
+        )
+        indices = torch.randint(
+            1, pool_size, (tokens, 1, topk), device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32
+        )
+        indices[..., -61:] = -1
+        return q, kv, indices, dim**-0.5
+
+    def test_one_hot_and_all_masked(self):
+        for heads, d_v, d_tail in ((8, 512, 0), (16, 256, 0), (32, 512, 64)):
+            with self.subTest(heads=heads, d_v=d_v, d_tail=d_tail):
+                q, kv, indices, scale = self._inputs(heads, d_v, d_tail)
+                indices.fill_(-1)
+                selected = torch.tensor([1, 5, 17, 31, 63], device="cuda")
+                indices[:, 0, 0] = selected.int()
+                actual = tilelang_sparse_fwd(q, kv, indices, scale, d_v).squeeze(0)
+                expected = kv.float()[selected, 0, :d_v][:, None].expand_as(actual)
+                torch.testing.assert_close(
+                    actual.float(), expected, atol=1e-3, rtol=1e-3
+                )
+
+                indices.fill_(-1)
+                empty = tilelang_sparse_fwd(q, kv, indices, scale, d_v)
+                self.assertTrue(torch.isfinite(empty).all().item())
+                self.assertEqual(torch.count_nonzero(empty).item(), 0)
+
+    def test_spread_and_wrong_index_negative_control(self):
+        q, kv, indices, scale = self._inputs(8, 512, 0)
+        actual = tilelang_sparse_fwd(q, kv, indices, scale, 512).squeeze(0).float()
+        expected = _reference(q.to(kv.dtype), kv, indices, scale, 512)
+        error = (actual - expected).abs().max() / expected.abs().max()
+        self.assertLess(error.item(), 0.04)
+
+        wrong = torch.where(indices >= 0, (indices + 2048) % 4096, indices)
+        incorrect = tilelang_sparse_fwd(q, kv, wrong, scale, 512).squeeze(0).float()
+        wrong_error = (incorrect - expected).abs().max() / expected.abs().max()
+        self.assertGreater(wrong_error.item(), 0.04)
+
+    def test_scaled_packed_rows_rejected(self):
+        q, _, indices, scale = self._inputs(8, 512, 0)
+        scaled_rows = torch.zeros(
+            4096, 1, 528, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn
+        )
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "raw KV rows"):
+            tilelang_sparse_fwd(q, scaled_rows, indices, scale, 512)
+
+    def test_rocm_fp8_format_rejected_on_cuda(self):
+        q, _, indices, scale = self._inputs(8, 512, 0)
+        kv = torch.empty(4096, 1, 512, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fnuz)
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "requires float8_e4m3fn"):
+            tilelang_sparse_fwd(q, kv, indices, scale, 512)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

+"""Raw FP8 allocation, fused paged write and PD buffer byte descriptors."""
+
+import unittest
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.memory_pool import MLATokenToKVPool
+from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_parallel, publish, reset_context
+from sglang.srt.server_args import ServerArgs
+from sglang.srt.utils import is_hip
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=10, stage="base-b", runner_config="1-gpu-small")
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(torch.cuda.is_available() and not is_hip(), "CUDA pool required")
+class TestTileLangRawFp8Pool(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        super().setUp()
+        reset_context()
+        self.addCleanup(reset_context)
+        publish(ServerArgs(model_path="dummy"), role="test")
+
+    def test_raw_write_round_trip_and_buffer_lengths(self):
+        for dim_nope, dim_rope in ((256, 0), (512, 0), (512, 64)):
+            with self.subTest(dim_nope=dim_nope, dim_rope=dim_rope):
+                pool = MLATokenToKVPool(
+                    size=128,
+                    page_size=64,
+                    dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn,
+                    kv_lora_rank=dim_nope,
+                    qk_rope_head_dim=dim_rope,
+                    layer_num=1,
+                    device="cuda",
+                    enable_memory_saver=False,
+                    use_dsa=True,
+                )
+                self.assertFalse(pool.dsa_kv_cache_store_fp8)
+                positions = torch.tensor(
+                    [1, 63, 64, 127], device="cuda", dtype=torch.int64
+                )
+                nope = torch.randn(4, 1, dim_nope, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+                rope = (
+                    torch.randn(4, 1, dim_rope, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+                    if dim_rope
+                    else None
+                )
+                with get_parallel().override(attn_dcp_size=1):
+                    pool._write_mla_kv_buffer(pool.kv_buffer[0], positions, nope, rope)
+                torch.cuda.synchronize()
+                expected = nope if rope is None else torch.cat((nope, rope), dim=-1)
+                actual = pool.get_key_buffer(0)[positions].float()
+                torch.testing.assert_close(
+                    actual, expected.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn).float(), atol=0, rtol=0
+                )
+                untouched = pool.get_key_buffer(0)[0].float()
+                self.assertEqual(torch.count_nonzero(untouched).item(), 0)
+                _, lengths, page_bytes = pool.get_contiguous_buf_infos()
+                width = dim_nope + dim_rope
+                self.assertEqual(lengths, [(128 + 64) * width])
+                self.assertEqual(page_bytes, [64 * width])
+                del pool
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
